Header: 2025-11-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Recording ID: fireflies-20251112-orion-POC-89234
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood CSM); Ravi Kapoor (CTO - Orion), Elena Martinez (Head of ML), Samir Dutta (DevOps), Priya Shah (Product)

Summary auto-gen: medium quality transcript. Notes: focus on per-token economics and benchmark scope.

00:00:03 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we, we really appreciate you taking the time. quick who we have on the call?
00:00:10 Ravi Kapoor: hi this is ravi, elena and samir are here and priya. we'll be the core team for the POC.
00:00:14 Maya Chen: awesome, i'll hand off to liam for a quick agenda then we'll dig into sizing and costs, is that ok?
00:00:20 Liam Patel: yeah hi all, quick agenda: 1) goals & success criteria, 2) workload and traffic profile, 3) benchmark plan (latency/throughput/cost), 4) deliverables and timeline. we'll focus heavily on unit economics — per-token estimates and how batching/caching affect that.
00:00:38 Elena Martinez: perfect. our main goal is to validate that we can run our chat summarization pipeline within a hard budget and meet a latency SLO of sub-300ms p95 for short sessions.
00:00:47 Maya Chen: got it. can you give us a sense of your current stack and where inference is today?
00:00:52 Elena Martinez: sure. currently we do onboarded transcriptions and an internal transformer model on prem, but for scaled chat experiences we hit cost spikes. we send about 15k sessions per day, avg tokens per session around 550, peak QPS around 45.
00:01:08 Samir Dutta: the infra is a mix of k8s clusters with GPUs (A10s) and some CPU fallback; security requires VPC peering for any private deployment.
00:01:17 Liam Patel: thanks, that helps. rough back-of-envelope: 15k sessions * 550 tokens = ~8.25M tokens/day. with a generation token ratio ~0.6 (so say 60% generation vs prompt), call it 5M generated tokens/day, ballpark. does that align?
00:01:37 Elena Martinez: yeah that's close, but our peak hour is heavy — 40% of traffic in a 2 hour window.
00:01:44 Maya Chen: okay, from the POC POV we'll want to test both baseline hosted and a dedicated (reserved) config; the cost per token shifts a lot with batching and KV cache hit rate.
00:01:55 Ravi Kapoor: can you explain the batching caching knobs? we heard batching reduces latency sometimes but increases throughput efficiency?
00:02:02 Liam Patel: sure — two levers. batching groups concurrent requests into a single matrix operation so GPUs are utilized better; that lowers per-token compute cost but can increase tail latency if requests wait to fill a batch. Redwood's runtime supports adaptive batching with latency caps. second is prefix/KV caching: if users share common prefixes or if session histories are hot, we can reuse KV cache entries so repeated tokens don't recompute, dramatically reducing per-token cost for follow-ups.
00:02:30 Priya Shah: our flows have a lot of repeated system prompts and clarifying questions, so caching might help. what's a realistic cache hit rate?
00:02:36 Liam Patel: at first POC we conservatively plan 10-20% hit; in optimized flows it can hit 40-60% depending on UX. for cost modeling we usually run scenarios: no cache, 20% hit, 40% hit.
00:02:47 Elena Martinez: ok that range is helpful. what about quantization — does that change latency/cost?
00:02:52 Liam Patel: yes — moving from fp16 to 4-bit quantized kernels can reduce GPU memory and increase throughput; unit cost per token can drop ~20-40% depending on model and hardware. but quality checks are essential; we'll include a quality guardrail in the POC.
00:03:08 Maya Chen: let's talk numbers — we've prepared a baseline per-token estimate for the model family you mentioned (opt-30b style). rough hosted per-gen-token estimate: $0.0006 — that's with moderate batching and minimal cache. with dedicated reserved capacity and optimized batching + quantization we can get unit cost down to $0.00018 - $0.00025 per gen-token.
00:03:30 Ravi Kapoor: okay so approximate daily gen token cost at 5M tokens/day is... hosted ~ $3k/day? that seems high.
00:03:38 Liam Patel: math: 5M * $0.0006 = $3,000/day yes; dedicated optimized at $0.0002 would be $1,000/day. The POC will help us determine if we can hit the optimized range; sometimes batching/config changes and lower-cost model variants (quantized +/- distilled) reduce cost further.
00:03:55 Elena Martinez: what's the tradeoff on latency when going for the $0.0002 per token? would we break the 300ms p95 goal?
00:04:02 Liam Patel: depends on request size and batch window. Our adaptive batching tries to cap waits so p95 stays within SLOs for moderate QPS. For those short sessions, if batch windows are small and KV cache hit is decent, we can likely meet 300ms p95. but we'll verify in bench.
00:04:19 Priya Shah: what's the benchmark plan look like?
00:04:22 Liam Patel: plan: 1) Redwood runs 2-hour synthetic run using your prompt-set and traffic profile against hosted endpoint and a dedicated infra config; 2) measure latencies (p50/p95/p99), throughput, GPU utilization, and token cost; 3) run quality eval on sampled outputs for regressions. We'll provide a benchmark runbook and shared spreadsheet so you can reproduce.
00:04:39 Jordan Reyes: i'll coordinate the logistics for the run and share the privacy-safe runbook.
00:04:44 Ravi Kapoor: do you need access to our environment for the dedicated test? we prefer to keep everything in our VPC for the dedicated pilot.
00:04:50 Maya Chen: we can do both — hosted endpoints for quick validation and a VPC-connected or private deployment for the dedicated run. for VPC we will need a short window of peering or a temporary bastion for metrics collection. we provide an infra checklist.
00:05:05 Samir Dutta: okay we can provide peering; however security needs SOC2 scope and KMS integration details.
00:05:12 Maya Chen: understood — we'll attach SOC2 docs and our KMS integration guide.
00:05:15 Elena Martinez: timeline — what does the POC cadence look like?
00:05:18 Liam Patel: typical POC: week 0 onboarding + data prep, week 1 hosted baseline run, week 2 dedicated config run, week 3 analysis and tuning, week 4 final report + decision. since you're targeting a production pilot by end of December, this maps okay but we'll need your prompt set and traffic data by Friday to hit the week-of-11-17 benchmark.
00:05:38 Priya Shah: that's tight but doable. budget-wise, we have an internal monthly budget target equivalent to ~$30k/mo for inference for this product. if the dedicated optimized cost is $1k/day that's ~$30k/mo — fits, but we need to ensure N+1 for spikes.
00:05:55 Liam Patel: good to call that out — for spikes we recommend burst capacity or autoscaling policies; reserved capacity covers baseline and we can enable burst-on-demand. that can be modeled as an incremental cost in the spreadsheet.
00:06:06 Ravi Kapoor: what about storage/retention token counts for embeddings or logging — extra costs?
00:06:11 Maya Chen: logs and embeddings are additional; we usually model them separately — for this POC we'll focus on generation token costs and add a conservative 10% overhead for logs/embeddings until you share exact volumes.
00:06:22 Elena Martinez: any tips to reduce cost during POC?
00:06:25 Liam Patel: yes: 1) canonicalize prompts to reduce prompt token length, 2) increase batching for background jobs, 3) use caching aggressively for repeated prefixes, 4) test lower-cost model variants for similarity-based tasks. We'll include a recommendations section in the spreadsheet.
00:06:40 Maya Chen: ok let's align on success criteria — what's a pass/fail for you?
00:06:44 Elena Martinez: pass = achieve avg production latency p95 <300ms for short sessions, total monthly inference cost under $30k with <5% quality regression vs current model.
00:06:55 Ravi Kapoor: also require SOC2 + KMS integration validated for any private deployment.
00:06:59 Maya Chen: noted. we'll capture that in the POC acceptance criteria.
00:07:03 Jordan Reyes: quick note — we'll log everything into the shared doc and I'll create a meeting invite for the benchmark kickoff.
00:07:08 Priya Shah: are there any gotchas for model compatibility? we use a few tokenizers and custom special tokens.
00:07:14 Liam Patel: good question — we sometimes see tokenizer mismatches. please include example tokenization and we can validate locally before the run. also note that some quantized kernels behave slightly differently on special tokens; we'll include a QA pass for that.
00:07:28 Elena Martinez: ok. for benchmarks, can you provide an expected cost range table?
00:07:33 Maya Chen: yes we'll send a spreadsheet with scenarios: columns for model variant, batch sizes, cache hit rates (0/20/40%), quantization option, hosted vs dedicated per-token cost, and total monthly estimate.
00:07:45 Ravi Kapoor: great. any competitor concerns we should be aware of? we have legal asking about data exposure to third parties — they flagged Anthropic and OpenAI as higher risk for our use-case.
00:07:55 Maya Chen: we'll include the private deployment option and note that with Private (VPC/on-prem) data never leaves your network, KMS integration included.
00:08:03 Elena Martinez: last question on benchmarks — how do you measure cost per token? is it directly from infra utilization or an estimated cost model?
00:08:10 Liam Patel: it's a combination — we measure actual GPU utilization, tokens produced during runs, and map that to compute cost for the infra used; for hosted endpoints we use Redwood's per-unit pricing. The spreadsheet will show both measured cost and modeled projections for scale.
00:08:25 Maya Chen: ok to recap and next steps — 1) Redwood sends cost-model spreadsheet and benchmark runbook (Maya + Liam) by 2025-11-14; 2) Orion shares prompt set, tokenization examples, and traffic profile by 2025-11-14 (Elena + Samir); 3) schedule benchmark week of 2025-11-17 — Jordan will send the invite; 4) Redwood sends SOC2 & KMS docs.
00:08:47 Ravi Kapoor: sounds good. will you include estimated costs for burst capacity?
00:08:51 Maya Chen: yes we'll include a separate row for burst sizing and estimated incremental cost.
00:08:55 Priya Shah: thanks, that covers our questions.
00:08:58 Maya Chen: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up over email with the attachments. tuning notes will follow after the first run.
00:09:05 Elena Martinez: great thanks.
